4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

## Objective
- Improve and validate the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Deliver changes in the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the project structure, game entry point, styles, and README.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes; no files were changed.

### Active
- Implement and validate archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining game UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement the requested mechanics and fix any discovered issues.
3. Run available checks, launch the game, and perform a visual check with a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`, `startup.sh`: Startup scripts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `Agents.md`: Project workflow notes.

## Important Context
- The game is a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project with no `package.json`.
- `app.js` describes GENESIS as a deterministic, multiscale educational model; it already includes genomes, cell plates, and research content.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

- Improve and validate the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Deliver changes in the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Read portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and the startup and capture scripts; no files were changed.

### Active
- Inspect the remaining game UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Implement and validate archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game UI and state/action logic.
2. Implement the requested mechanics and fix any discovered issues.
3. Run available checks, launch the game, and perform a visual check with a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.

- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- The game is a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project with no `package.json`.
- `app.js` describes GENESIS as a deterministic, multiscale educational model; it already includes genomes, cell plates, and research content.

8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

2:

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Deliver changes in the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and the project structure.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Confirmed no files have been changed so far.

### Active
- Inspect remaining game UI and state/action logic.
- Implement and validate archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement the requested mechanics and fix any discovered issues.
3. Run available checks, launch the game, and perform a visual check with a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- The game is a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project with no `package.json`.
- `app.js` describes GENESIS as a deterministic, multiscale educational model; it already includes genomes, cell plates, and research content.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` already adds live or archived genome-derived cells to the plate.
- `archiveView()` renders saved genomes with “SEED WORLD” and download controls; inspect the rest of the implementation before changing behavior.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.

## Decisions

### Active

- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Deliver changes in the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.

### Active
- Inspect remaining game UI and state/action logic.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks and visually validate the game.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement the requested mechanics and fix any discovered issues.
3. Run available checks, launch the game, and perform a visual check with a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- The game is a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project with no `package.json`.
- `app.js` describes GENESIS as a deterministic, multiscale educational model; it already includes genomes, cell plates, and research content.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells to the plate.
- `archiveView()` renders saved genomes with “SEED WORLD” and download controls; inspect the rest of the implementation before changing behavior.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, and `start.sh`.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Found `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` and an archive view with “SEED WORLD” and download controls.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and game state/action logic.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks and visually validate the game.

### Blocked
- A shell-tool call failed because its `command` argument was missing; retry with a valid call.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement requested mechanics and address discovered bugs.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `app.js` describes GENESIS as a deterministic, multiscale educational model with genomes, cell plates, and research content.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- The archive view renders saved genomes with “SEED WORLD” and download controls.

- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Confirmed the existing archive view has “SEED WORLD” and download controls; `saveGenome()` archives a sequenced genome and prevents duplicate archives.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through the `add-element-plate` action.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and game state/action logic.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.

- `README.md`: Project overview.

- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes and `git status --short` is clean.
- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, `README.md`, and `Agents.md`.
- Confirmed the archive view has “SEED WORLD” and download controls; `saveGenome()` archives sequenced genomes and prevents duplicates.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through the `add-element-plate` action.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate with a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement requested mechanics and address discovered bugs.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- Archive flow uses `saveGenome()`; simulation actions are handled by `handleAction()`.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg` exists, but no visual inspection was recorded.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes and `git status --short` is clean.
- Confirmed the archive view has “SEED WORLD” and download controls; `saveGenome()` archives sequenced genomes and prevents duplicates.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through the `add-element-plate` action.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate with a latest JPEG screenshot if appropriate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement requested mechanics and address discovered bugs.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- Archive flow uses `saveGenome()`; simulation actions are handled by `handleAction()`.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg` exists, but no visual inspection was recorded.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- `node --check app.js` passed; `git status --short` was clean at the last check.
- Confirmed the archive view has “SEED WORLD” and download controls; `saveGenome()` archives sequenced genomes and prevents duplicates.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through the `add-element-plate` action.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.
- Reviewed portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, `start.sh`, and `capture.sh`.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement requested mechanics and address discovered bugs.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- Archive flow uses `saveGenome()`; simulation actions are handled by `handleAction()`.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the archive view has “SEED WORLD” and download controls; `saveGenome()` archives sequenced genomes and prevents duplicates.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through the `add-element-plate` action.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Inspected the beginning of `app.js`, part of its UI/state logic, and `index.html`.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Implement archival and cell-integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement requested mechanics and address discovered bugs.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- Archive flow uses `saveGenome()`; simulation actions are handled by `handleAction()`.
- Repository was clean at the last status check.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the archive view includes “SEED WORLD” and genome download controls; `saveGenome()` blocks duplicate genome IDs.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through the `add-element-plate` action.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Inspected core state, plate simulation, genome archive, lab, and action logic in `app.js`; no new code changes made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI and state/action logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue examining remaining UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Implement the requested mechanics and fix any discovered bugs.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- Archive flow uses `saveGenome()`; simulation actions are handled by `handleAction()`.
- `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna`; `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, so verify and resolve the archive eligibility mismatch.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No new implementation decisions recorded.

## Work State

### Completed
- Confirmed the archive view includes “SEED WORLD” and genome download controls; `saveGenome()` blocks duplicate genome IDs.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through `add-element-plate`.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Inspected core state, plate simulation, genome archive, lab, action logic, and portions of `app.js` and `index.html`; no code changes made.

### Active
- Resolve the archive eligibility mismatch: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, while `saveGenome()` checks `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Inspect remaining UI and action handlers, then run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Fix genome archive eligibility and implement the requested mechanics.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`; `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`.
- The current element guide describes plate element markers as visual-only and says they do not model chemical reactions or biological effects.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State

### Completed
- Confirmed the archive view includes “SEED WORLD” and genome download controls; `saveGenome()` blocks duplicate genome IDs.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through `add-element-plate`.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Inspected core state, plate simulation, genome archive, lab, action logic, and portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; no code changes made.
- Confirmed the working tree was clean at the latest status check.

### Active
- Resolve the archive eligibility mismatch: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, while `saveGenome()` checks `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Inspect remaining UI and action handlers, then run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Fix genome archive eligibility and implement the requested mechanics.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`; `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`.
- The current element guide describes plate element markers as visual-only and says they do not model chemical reactions or biological effects.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions recorded.

## Work State

### Completed
- Confirmed the archive view includes “SEED WORLD” and genome download controls; `saveGenome()` blocks duplicate genome IDs.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through `add-element-plate`.
- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; identified that element markers are explicitly visual-only and do not affect cell metrics.
- `node --check app.js` passed; working tree was clean at the latest status check.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, while `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate after implementation.

### Blocked
- None.

1. Inspect remaining UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Fix genome archive eligibility and implement the requested mechanics.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`; `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`.

- No code changes have been made.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the archive view includes “SEED WORLD” and genome download controls; `saveGenome()` blocks duplicate genome IDs.
- Confirmed plate cells can record sandbox element markers through `add-element-plate`.
- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; element markers are visual-only and do not affect cell metrics.
- `node --check app.js` passed; `git status --short` returned no output at the latest check.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, while `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate after implementation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Fix genome archive eligibility and implement the requested mechanics.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`; `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`.
- The element guide says plate element markers are visual-only and do not model chemical reactions or biological effects.
- No code changes have been made.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected portions of `app.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; confirmed plate element markers are visual-only and do not affect cell metrics.
- `node --check app.js` passed; `git status --short` was clean at the latest check.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg` (1200×900); no visual findings were recorded.

### Active
- Fix genome archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, while `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate after implementation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Fix genome archive eligibility and implement the requested mechanics.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`; `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`.
- The element guide says plate element markers are visual-only and do not model chemical reactions or biological effects.
- No code changes have been made.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected `app.js` and `index.html` for initial game state and mechanics.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passed before changes.

### Active
- Fix genome archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, while `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue inspecting UI and action handlers in `index.html` and `app.js`.
2. Fix genome archive eligibility and implement the requested mechanics.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds live or archived genome-derived cells.
- `saveGenome()` checks `S.samples.dna`; sequencing sets `S.samples.sequenced`.
- The element guide says plate element markers are visual-only and do not model chemical reactions or biological effects.
- A background inspection of mechanics was started; its findings were not yet returned.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e433bd04affeCqkv8gzMwJrBC5" state="completed">
## Verified findings

- **Archive navigation:** The application shell includes a Genome archive entry in [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html ).

- **Plate population and lineage:** In [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js ), `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived, count)` adds up to six cells per call, subject to a 30-cell plate cap. Archive-sourced additions are labeled separately. `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome from `plateSources`, then the archive, and finally the current genome as a fallback.

- **Division and checkpoints:** `dividePlateCell(cell)` refuses division for viruses, cells whose `cycleProgress` is below 1, or cells that fail `cycleCheckpoint`. The checkpoint considers apoptosis, senescence, ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and viability. `updateCellState(cell)` derives the displayed state from viability, age/divisions, damage, ROS, protein load, and membrane integrity.

- **Action handlers:** The `cell-cycle` action lowers ATP, sets cycle progress to 1, checks the checkpoint, and may add a daughter cell. `stain` records a fluorescence proxy based on viability and membrane condition. A selected cell can be removed only if at least one cell remains on the plate.

- **Element annotations:** The `add-element-plate` action increments a stored marker count and briefly adds a visual halo. These markers are persistent annotations, not modeled exposures: they do not change cell metrics or predict real-cell responses. The interface’s explanatory copy states this limitation.

- **Visual effects:** `plateCellMarkup(cell)` derives color hue and pulse speed from genome traits and applies visual classes for selection, archived lineage, stress, staining, and marker exposure. [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css ) styles the pulse, stress, stain, archive, selection, and element-halo effects. The pulse animation is disabled for users who prefer reduced motion.

## Educational caveat and safe design opportunities

The plate is a simplified, rule-based visualization—not a validated biological or chemical model. In particular, adding an element marker should not be presented as dosing a cell or causing a biological reaction. The existing explanatory copy helps establish that distinction.

Potential clarity improvements, without changing the mechanics, include labeling cell-cycle outcomes and fluorescence as **simulation/proxy results**, keeping archive lineage visibly distinct, and explaining that marker count and halo are annotations rather than exposure levels or predicted effects.
</subagent>

<subagent sessionID="ses_e433f4e81ffe5qNKFHJyhkt938" state="completed" description="Map game mechanics and handlers">
## Findings

- **State and persistence —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:3,49–55`  
  State is saved in `localStorage` under `genesis-living-genome-v1`. A new world initializes the genome, environment, simulation, and plate; saved state is restored on load with simulation paused. The startup code also fills in defaults for plate cells and research progress. `newWorld()` at line 115 retains the archive and researcher progress, but resets the notebook.

- **Simulation and evolution —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:84–87,136`  
  `tick()` advances world and plate-cell metrics, runs a generation step every 25 ticks, and saves state every 4 ticks. The interval runs every 650 ms, with speed controlling ticks per interval. `generationStep()` at lines 85–86 creates a mutated genome and records generation history. The “Advance 10 generations” action in `handleAction()` advances ten generations directly.

- **Cell observatory —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:63–83,103,136`  
  Plate-cell genomes, division, and ongoing cell updates are handled by `mutatePlateGenome()`, `dividePlateCell()`, and `advancePlateCells()`. Cells can be added from the live genome or archive; the plate is capped at 30. `handleAction()` covers cell-cycle advancement, staining, removal, and genome inspection.

- **Lab and sequencing —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:118–134`  
  `sample()` makes both DNA and RNA available. `runLab()` enforces DNA prerequisites for PCR, gel electrophoresis, Sanger, whole-genome sequencing, and CRISPR simulation, and an RNA prerequisite for gene expression assays. `doSequence()` requires DNA, assembles the simulated sequence, records a notebook entry, and awards research progress.

- **Archive and file workflows —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:111,115–116,135–139`  
  `saveGenome()` archives the current genome; export downloads an archive/notebook JSON wrapper, while import accepts a genome object (either at the root or under `genome`). **As implemented, importing the database JSON produced by export will fail validation:** the importer checks for `genes` and `sequence` on the wrapper, but the exported wrapper has `archive` and `notebook`.

- **Verified archive prerequisite mismatch —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:116,118`  
  `saveGenome()` displays “Sequence the genome before archiving it,” but checks only `S.samples.dna`, not `S.samples.sequenced`. Since `sample()` sets `S.samples.dna = true`, collecting a sample is sufficient to archive without running `doSequence()`.

- **App shell and navigation —** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:18–29,37–44`  
  The HTML defines navigation for the main views and research sections, the top-bar world controls, and the view/modal/toast containers; it loads `app.js` at the end of the body.

No files were modified.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Keep element markers as visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected `app.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, and `README.md`; `node --check app.js` passed before changes.
- Mapped archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, and action-handler mechanics; identified genome archive eligibility and export/import format mismatches.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, but `saveGenome()` currently gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining action handlers and UI to define integration points.
2. Implement archive and cell-part integration, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct the archive prerequisite and export/import mismatch.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `saveGenome()` says “Sequence the genome before archiving it.” but checks `S.samples.dna`, not `S.samples.sequenced`; `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Element guide and plate markers are explicitly visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Keep element markers as visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected core files and mapped archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, and action-handler mechanics.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passed before changes.
- Identified archive eligibility/state and export/import format mismatches.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, but `saveGenome()` gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining action handlers and UI to define integration points.
2. Implement archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct the archive prerequisite and export/import mismatch.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome, archived=false, count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg` is a 1200×900 JPEG.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.

### Completed

- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passed before changes.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, but `saveGenome()` gates on `S.samples.dna`.

- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

- (none)

- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected core files and mapped archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, and action-handler mechanics.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passed before changes.
- Identified archive eligibility/state and export/import format mismatches.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, but `saveGenome()` gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining action handlers and UI to define integration points.
2. Implement archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct the archive prerequisite and export/import mismatch.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- Repository was clean at the time checked; no changes have been made yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, and action-handler mechanics.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passed before changes.
- Identified archive eligibility/state and export/import format mismatches.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling: `doSequence()` sets `S.samples.sequenced`, but `saveGenome()` gates on `S.samples.dna`.
- Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining action handlers and UI to define integration points.
2. Implement archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct the archive prerequisite and export/import mismatch.
3. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
4. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- No changes had been made at the last repository check.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes and the repository was clean at an earlier status check.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the latest status check; no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes and the repository was clean at the latest status check; no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits; the latest inspection found no changes made.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes; repository was clean at the latest status check, with no implementation changes made.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.
