messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the latest status check; no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed and add procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes.
- Confirmed `git status --short` was clean at the time checked.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.

- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes and `git status --short` was clean when last checked.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes and `git status --short` was clean when last checked.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passed earlier; `git status --short` was clean before the current inspection.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive currently supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make cell reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the start of the inspection.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the start; no changes have been made.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the start; no changes have been made.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility/state handling and implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and procedural effects; correct archive prerequisites and export/import compatibility.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.
- `start.sh`: Startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.

16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility and state handling; implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and archive prerequisite and export/import fixes.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics, and current code does not model chemistry or reactions.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e431efa58ffe3gcjgpWx0TNdPq" state="completed">
## Findings

No files were changed. The main integration point is `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js`; the genome archive, cell observatory, sequencing, and import/export flows are all implemented there.

### Archive and sequencing flow

- `sample()` sets both DNA and RNA sample flags. `doSequence()` then builds `S.genome.sequence` with `genomeSequence()`, marks `S.samples.sequenced = true`, and records the sequencing result.
- `saveGenome()` is the archive gate. It checks **`S.samples.dna`**, not `S.samples.sequenced`, and stores a copy of the current genome in `S.archive`. This means DNA extraction alone can allow archiving, despite the UI prompting users to sequence first.
- `genomeSequence()` assembles the model sequence from each gene’s promoter, enhancer, coding sequence, and intron, then appends the genome’s noncoding sequence. `makeGene()` supplies the modeled coding and regulatory fields.
- `newWorld(source)` starts a new world from an archived genome when one is provided. `makeGenome()` copies the source’s genes, chromosome count, generation, and mutation count, while generating new noncoding sequence and a new genome ID.
- `addCellsToPlate()` stores a genome copy in `S.plateSources` and uses it to seed plate cells. The `plate-archive` action in `handleAction()` calls it for an archived selection; `plateGenome()` resolves the genome used to display and simulate each cell.

**Parts implication:** Existing archived genes are already reusable as modeled parts through the genome’s `genes` array. New kinds of parts or metadata need an explicit place in the archive schema and seed/plate paths; otherwise `makeGenome()` will not necessarily preserve them. Rebuilding the sequence from genes and newly generated noncoding sequence also means an imported or archived sequence may not match a newly seeded world’s sequence.

### Export/import mismatch

- `archiveView()` offers database export and import, plus per-genome downloads.
- The `export` action downloads an object shaped like `{format, archive, notebook}`. `download-genome` instead downloads an individual genome object.
- The import change handler accepts `data.genome || data`, then checks for `genes` and `sequence`. Consequently, it accepts individual genome files and `{genome: ...}` wrappers, but **does not accept the database export it creates**: that object has `archive`, not top-level `genes` or `genome`.
- Import adds the supplied genome to the front of the archive and stamps a save date. It does not check for duplicates or validate the shape of the genome’s fields beyond the two required properties.

This is the clearest compatibility fix point: make import recognize the exported database format and define how to merge its archive and notebook, or change export to emit a format the current importer accepts.

### Educational reaction model and procedural effects

- `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies such as ATP, ROS, damage, membrane integrity, and viability from modeled traits and environment. `tick()` similarly updates whole-world proxies. These are integration points for a **clearly bounded educational reaction model**, if one is added.
- Element exposure currently does not participate in those calculations. `elementResultMarkup()` and the `add-element-plate` action describe the exposure as a visual-only marker; the action increments `elementExposures`, adds a brief halo, and leaves cell metrics unchanged.
- For presentation-only effects, `plateCellMarkup()` derives a cell’s visual classes and styling from its state. The cell view’s element panel and its handler are the corresponding UI entry points.

The app already signals the intended scope: Codex text calls model readouts educational proxies, while the element panel explicitly says it does not model chemistry, reactions, or biological effects. Any new reaction/effect behavior should retain that distinction rather than imply real biological prediction.

### Main risks

1. **Archive eligibility contradicts the prompt:** saving checks DNA extraction, not successful sequencing.
2. **Export cannot round-trip through import:** full-database backups are rejected by the current import shape check.
3. **Imported records are weakly validated:** duplicate entries are allowed, and fields used later by rendering, seeding, and sequence generation may be absent or malformed.
4. **Custom parts may be lost:** seeding copies genes but regenerates noncoding DNA; any added part data needs explicit propagation and a defined relationship to the assembled sequence.
5. **UI scope can outpace model scope:** adding visual reactions without keeping them separate from metrics would conflict with the current visual-only disclosure. Conversely, adding metric effects requires carefully labeling them as model assumptions rather than biological predictions.
6. **Imported text is rendered in archive markup:** archive fields such as ID and species are interpolated into HTML without visible escaping, so imported values should be treated as untrusted display data.

### Relevant files

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js` — genome construction and sequencing (`makeGene()`, `makeGenome()`, `genomeSequence()`, `doSequence()`); persistence and archive (`storeState()`, `loadState()`, `saveGenome()`, `archiveView()`); world/plate seeding (`newWorld()`, `plateGenome()`, `addCellsToPlate()`); reaction-model entry points (`advancePlateCells()`, `tick()`, `elementResultMarkup()`, `handleAction()`); import handler.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` — app shell and navigation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css` — presentation and procedural visual styling.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility and state handling; implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Correct the archive export/import format mismatch.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/integration mechanics, research-informed reactions, and archive prerequisite and export/import fixes.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate using a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite telling users to sequence first.
- Export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`; current importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`, so exported database JSON fails validation.
- Genome archive supports saving genomes and seeding new worlds; archived genomes can also seed observatory plate cells.
- The lab’s `CRISPR edit simulation` directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics, and current code does not model chemistry or reactions.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

- Make reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility and import/export handling; implement DNA and cell-part archival and incorporation.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects, consistent with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/incorporation mechanics, research-informed reactions, and archive prerequisite and import/export fixes.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and validate with a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite prompting users to sequence first.
- Archive export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`, while the importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`; exported database JSON therefore fails validation.
- Archived genomes can seed new worlds or observatory plate cells; there is no cell-part archive/incorporation flow yet.
- The lab’s CRISPR simulation directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- Element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics, and current code does not model chemistry or reactions.
- `cellView()` renders cell components and genome-derived traits.

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.

## Objective
- Improve and validate GENESIS so players can archive DNA sequences and cell parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make reactions research-informed, add procedural effects, and fix bugs and clean up code.

## Requirements
- Check that the game runs correctly, fix bugs, and clean up code.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not simulated doses or biological reactions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected archive, import/export, lab, cell-plate, action-handler, and UI integration points.

### Active
- Fix archive eligibility and import/export handling; implement DNA and cell-part archival and incorporation.
- Add research-informed reactions and procedural effects, consistent with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, launch the game, and visually validate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cell-part archival/incorporation mechanics, research-informed reactions, and archive prerequisite and import/export fixes.
2. Run checks, launch the game, and validate with a JPEG no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, test results, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, mechanics, rendering, archive, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript project; no `package.json`.
- `addCellsToPlate(genome,archived=false,count=6)` adds genome-derived cells; plate capacity is 30.
- `sample()` makes DNA/RNA available and `doSequence()` marks sequencing complete; `saveGenome()` currently checks `S.samples.dna` despite prompting users to sequence first.
- Archive export wraps data in `archive` and `notebook`, while the importer expects a genome object with `genes` and `sequence`; exported database JSON therefore fails validation.
- Archived genomes can seed new worlds or observatory plate cells; there is no cell-part archive/incorporation flow yet.
- The lab’s CRISPR simulation directly changes a coding base, activity, mutations, sequence, and damage.
- The element guide and plate markers are visual-only; markers do not alter cell metrics, and current code does not model chemistry or reactions.
- Recent inspection reached `cellView()` in `app.js`; no implementation changes or validation were recorded.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version
